partners.mechanism_chain: NLRP3 (HGNC:7745) —DISRUPTS→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032669); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032669) —PRODUCES→ IL-1beta (UniProtKB:P01073); IL-1beta (UniProtKB:P01073) —INCREASES→ Inflammation (HP:0011420); IL-1beta (UniProtKB:P01073) —INCREASES→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365). Gain-of-function mutations in NLRP3 lead to its constitutive activation, resulting in the assembly and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. This process drives the maturation and release of IL-1beta. Elevated IL-1beta levels contribute to the inflammatory phenotype observed in familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome 1 and the inflammatory component of hearing loss, autosomal dominant 34. The chronic inflammation also impacts cochlear function, leading to hearing impairment.

partners.mechanism_chain: NLRP3 (HGNC:7970) —DISRUPTS→ Inflammasome activation (GO:0032655); Inflammasome activation (GO:0032655) —LEADS_TO→ Autoinflammation (HP:00114240); NFKB1 (HGNC:7754) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:270); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:270) —DECREASES→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); Inflammasome activation (GO:0032655) —INCREASES→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:270); Autoinflammation (HP:00114240) —LEADS_TO→ Cold-induced urticaria (HP:0030178). Mutations in NLRP3 lead to inflammasome activation and autoinflammation, characteristic of FCAS1, which can manifest as cold-induced urticaria. Separately, loss-of-function mutations in NFKB1 impair the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, leading to defective B cell maturation and common variable immunodeficiency (CVID12). The convergence occurs because inflammasome activation (NLRP3) leads to increased signaling through the NF-kappaB pathway, which is then impaired by NFKB1 mutations. Thus, dysregulation of NF-kappaB signaling is a shared node, albeit with different upstream causes and downstream consequences.
